rationale: The Latin anchor "radere" (to scrape/shave) and the specific attestation from Job 2:8 — where Job scrapes his sores with a potsherd ("testa saniem radebat") — point directly to the action of repeatedly scraping a surface, matching scrape.v.01 ("scratch repeatedly"). The context is physical and literal scraping of skin/sores, not cutting into a surface to inscribe (scrape.v.02) nor injuring skin incidentally (skin.v.02).
